blocks.text: Reading Islam through its own sources
A careful reading begins with context. Learn to distinguish what a text says, how it is interpreted and what a person believes.
Begin with the terms, sources and perspective needed to understand the subject. A named text, a later interpretation and an individual’s belief need to be identified separately.
Follow the whole passage and its surrounding discussion. Identify what it states, what an interpreter supplies and where readings differ.
One God: the shared starting point
Read the complete four-verse chapter. It confesses God’s oneness, rejects begetting and being begotten, and denies any equal to him.
Let careful description lead to a precise question. Link the Islamic background to the relevant Christian claim, so readers can move between understanding and comparison.
Conviction with an open Bible. Scripture first. Reformed convictions. Sources you can examine.
Rooted in Scripture. Open for discovery.
A place to read slowly, ask deeply, and follow the connections. Scripture, study and the voices of Christian history, brought together for a lifetime of learning.

Meet the authors. Explore the collection. Trace each work to its source.
